extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in 'universal' speech representation learning. It includes a new general-purpose massively multilingual evaluation dataset dubbed Fleurs in all of the 102 languages.
extraction.license: Permissive licenses that allow use and redistribution of the data for research purposes (specific licenses vary by constituent dataset)
extraction.creator: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.inLanguage: 102 languages from 10+ language families including Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, Austronesian, Dravidian, Turkic, Uralic, Atlantic-Congo, Kra-Dai, Austro-Asiatic, Kartvelian, Japonic, Koreanic, Mongolic, and Nilo-Saharan
extraction.citeAs: Conneau, A., Bapna, A., Zhang, Y., Ma, M., von Platen, P., Lozhkov, A., Cherry, C., Jia, Y., Rivera, C., Kale, M., Van Esch, D., Axelrod, V., Khanuja, S., Clark, J. H., Firat, O., Auli, M., Ruder, S., Riesa, J., & Johnson, M. (2022). XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations. arXiv:2203.10752v3 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S is a benchmark that aggregates multiple existing datasets and introduces a new dataset (Fleurs). Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark, using 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets in 102 languages. Between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2.3 on average). Other datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) are sourced from existing publicly available corpora.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on the platform. Average results are not expected to change significantly.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs is based on 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets in 102 languages. MLS is derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli contains speech from European Parliament sessions. CoVoST-2 is a large-scale multilingual speech translation corpus. Minds-14 is an intent classification dataset from the e-banking domain in 14 language varieties.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Training sets have around 10 hours of supervision. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For VoxPopuli, 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task were selected.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Scripts are provided to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps. For MLS, the official 10-hour splits provided by Pratap et al. are used to evaluate few-shot learning capabilities. For VoxPopuli, languages with more than 10 hours of data were selected. For speech retrieval, the pool of transcription candidates is augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia. Multilingual fine-tuning is used across tasks where specified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Fleurs uses parallel sentences from the FLoRes benchmark with between one and three speech recordings collected per sentence. Speech transcriptions and translations for VoxPopuli were collected from European Parliament sessions. CoVoST-2 provides speech-to-text translation annotations. Minds-14 contains intent labels from the e-banking domain.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between 1 and 3 recordings per sentence for Fleurs (2.3 on average); 1 evaluation run per task for most tasks; 1/5 evaluation runs for speech retrieval
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets in Fleurs
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and fine-tuning scripts are made easily accessible through the HuggingFace platform. A 2nd version of the Fleurs dataset is planned with fixes for missing or low-quality recordings. Additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions. A submission form will be provided where results can be double-checked for consistency before being added to the leaderboard. More details will be added on the XTREME-S Dataset card at https://hf.co/datasets/google/xtreme_s.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker identity information is present in the speech recordings. The benchmark notes that speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting on speaker ID, and that avoiding overfitting on speaker ID for the LangID task is essential for obtaining good performance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster. The benchmark aims to enable rapid access to data-efficient speech technology for all the world's languages, including low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli. Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is identified as an important research direction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech data is not abundant for all languages. FLEURS is complete at more than 97% with some missing or low-quality recordings. The benchmark covers 102 languages but not all of the world's approximately 6,900 languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluating cross-lingual speech representations across four task families: (1) Speech Recognition (ASR) using Fleurs, MLS, and VoxPopuli; (2) Speech Translation (ST) using CoVoST-2; (3) Speech Classification using Fleurs-LangID and Minds-14; (4) Speech Retrieval using Fleurs. It supports training, fine-tuning, and evaluation of multilingual speech models. The benchmark encourages data-efficient self-supervised representation learning and multilingual fine-tuning over monolingual fine-tuning.
